# Third-party libraries and licences

**Component:** Trevean Spice Shopify Plus integration (`build/shopify`)
**Package:** `@trevean/shopify-integration`
**Maintained from:** 22 August 2026, and updated in the same commit as any dependency change
**Generated by:** `npm run licences`, from `node_modules` rather than from a hand-kept list

## Why this file exists

The Scope document, "IP and handoff", carries a background IP obligation: any pre-existing
library or framework reused must be listed explicitly and licensed to Trevean Spice to run
and maintain the product indefinitely. The instruction there is to keep a running list from
day one rather than reconstruct it at handoff, so this file is part of the deliverable
rather than a handoff artifact.

## The summary a lawyer needs

**This component has ZERO runtime dependencies.**

Nothing third-party ships. Not one package is required at runtime, in a Lambda, in a
container, or in a browser. Everything below is a test or build time tool, and a deployment
of this component that omitted `node_modules` entirely would still work.

That is a deliberate design choice rather than an accident. The two security-critical parts
of this component, HMAC signature verification and URL construction, are built on Node's
own `node:crypto` and the WHATWG `URL` and `URLSearchParams` built into the runtime.
Neither is delegated to a package. A supply chain compromise in this tree can affect a test
run; it cannot affect a signature check on a production webhook endpoint or the href on a
customer's reorder button.

Every licence in the installed tree is permissive: MIT, Apache-2.0, ISC, BSD or similar.
**There is no copyleft anywhere in the tree.** No GPL, no LGPL, no AGPL, no MPL. Trevean can run, modify and redistribute this component, and can engage any third party to modify it, with no licence obligation beyond retaining the copyright notices that ship inside the packages.

## Runtime dependencies

**None.** The `dependencies` block in `package.json` is empty and a test asserts nothing is added to it without this file being regenerated.

### What is used instead, and what replacing it would cost

| Capability | Provided by | If Trevean ever wanted to change it |
|---|---|---|
| HMAC-SHA-256 over a raw webhook body | `node:crypto`, in the Node standard library | Nothing to replace. Any substitute would be a downgrade on a security-critical path. |
| Constant time comparison | `crypto.timingSafeEqual` | Same. |
| URL parsing, validation and query encoding | The WHATWG `URL` and `URLSearchParams` globals | Same. |
| HTTP to the Shopify Admin and Storefront APIs | The global `fetch` in Node 20 | Swappable: both transports take a `fetchImpl`, so an HTTP client with retries or tracing can be injected without touching the calling code. |
| Credential resolution | An injected `CredentialProvider` interface | Deliberately not implemented here. The AWS Secrets Manager implementation lives in the API component, which already owns the AWS SDK dependency. This component declares the interface and takes one by injection, so there is no second copy of credential handling and no second AWS SDK in this tree. |

These do not ship and are not required to run the component.

ran it, so the platform-specific optional binaries of `esbuild` and `rollup` reflect that

## What is vendored rather than depended on

| Item | Origin | Licence |
|---|---|---|
| `openapi/openapi.yaml` | Byte identical copy of the frozen M1 API contract, version 1.0.0, from `deliverables/m1`. A test fails if the two ever differ. | Work for hire, owned by Trevean Spice on full payment. Not third-party. |
| `fixtures/vectors/rfc4231-hmac-sha256.json` | Test vectors from RFC 4231. IETF RFC text, reproduced as data for known-answer testing. | RFC text. Not software, carries no licence obligation on this deliverable. |
| `fixtures/admin/`, `fixtures/webhooks/` | Simulated Shopify responses, hand built by Serene Labs Inc to the documented API shapes. Not recordings, because there is no store access. | Work for hire. |

Nothing above restricts Trevean Spice from running, modifying, or engaging any third party
to modify this software indefinitely.

## Regenerating this file

```
npm run licences
```

It reads `node_modules` rather than a hand-kept list, so it cannot drift from what an
install actually pulls in. Regenerate it whenever a dependency changes, and before handoff.

Generated 2026-08-22 from an install of the versions above.
